text:
kevin: Heads up — we started seeing inference p99 spike ~200ms on eastus2-gpu pool around 09:12 UTC, coincides with a host-level egress policy change. @sre-oncall can you look?

maria: Noticed packet drops on a handful of hosts, looks like an ingress/egress policing rule got applied. I grabbed tc on one of the noisy hosts.

kevin: paste the tc output pls

maria: ```
# tc qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc htb 1: root refcnt 2 r2q 10 default 30 direct_packets_stat 0
qdisc ingress ffff: parent ffff:fff1 ----------------
qdisc cake 8001: dev eth1 root refcnt 2 bandwidth 10Gbit diffserv3 triple-isolate
```

raj: That cake+htb mix is odd — we normally use cake alone on NICs with RDMA offload. Which provisioner run applied this?

node-provisioner-bot: deploy action: "apply-host-qos" by @olivia at 2026-03-12T09:10:54Z — config: "egress:police 800mbit; qdisc:htb+cake"

olivia: I pushed a quick QoS profile to limit noisy build traffic during a maintenance window. It targeted non-prod but the selector matched a GPU label due to a label typo (env: nonprd vs non-prod).

kevin: That explains why GPU inference pods were hit. Any packet loss stats?

maria: ran `tc -s qdisc` and `ethtool -S` — sample from host-az2-12:
```
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc htb 1: root
 Sent 123456789 bytes  recv 98765432 bytes
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
qdisc cake 8001: Sent 123450000 bytes  recv 98765000 bytes
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 12
 backlog 2000b 24p
Dropped 142 packets  (policed)

# ethtool -S eth0 | grep drop
rx_dropped: 0
tx_dropped: 138

# dmesg | tail -n 5
mlx5_core: VF VF0 flagged egress policing applied
```

olivia: ugh, sorry everyone. I rolled the change for non-prod but the label filter was `env: nonprd` and our GPU nodes use `env: non-prod`. Mistmatch meant the policy applied to both via legacy selector semantics.

raj: Is this causing RDMA fallback? If ML job sees TX drops it can incur retries which blow up token latency.

maria: Yes, we saw reconnects in logs and increased gdr copy fallback messages: `nv_peer_mem: falling back to tcp` on one host.

olivia: rolling back the host-qos change now. @deploy-bot can you cancel and revert?

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for action apply-host-qos (id: 0a3f2c). Reverting QoS profiles to previous state across eastus2.

kevin: While rollback runs, can we temporarily add an iptables rule to bypass policing for pods in the redwood-gpu namespace?

maria: I can add netfilter-based ACCEPT for those IP ranges, but netem policing happens at qdisc so iptables won't fully bypass. Better to remove the police class. Doing a targeted `tc class change` to set rate to max on affected hosts.

sre-oncall: I'll coordinate with oncall to sweep the rest of the cluster for accidentally-applied qos. Scripted grep for the bad selector: `kubectl get nodes -l env=nonprd` then map to hosts with `tc qdisc show` —I'll run it now.

maria: Patch applied to 6 hosts: `tc class change dev eth1 classid 1:10 htb rate 10000Mbit` — immediate drop in tx_dropped and p99 started falling.

olivia: I've opened a PR to tighten selector semantics and added an explicit `matchLabels` check; also adding an allowlist so GPU pools are excluded from any host-level egress policing by default. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-provisioner/pull/412

raj: Long term, we should prevent QoS changes from applying to NICs with RDMA-enabled flags. Maybe have provisioner query `ethtool -k` or node annotation `rdma=true` and skip.

maria: Agreed. Also adding a small synthetic probe that hits a pinned inference endpoint after any host-qos change and fails the change if p99 increases >50ms.

kevin: Thanks — keep this thread updated when rollback completes and when PR merges. Also want postmortem notes: incident window 09:10–09:32 UTC, impact: eastus2-gpu p99 token latency +200ms, ~6 hosts briefly policed.

deploy-bot: rollback completed at 2026-03-12T09:25:40Z — QoS profiles restored.

maria: final checks show tx_dropped back to 0, RDMA back online. Running cluster-wide search for `nonprd` label to catch other typos.

olivia: PR merged and scheduled for next safe deploy window with an integration test. Apologies for the disruption. :bow:

kevin: Closing once we have the postmortem doc — @maria can you create a short writeup and add links to the PR and commands used?

maria: Will do, summarizing actions and remediation steps now.

sre-oncall: Confirmed last_message_ts: 1795008844 — closing monitoring alerts.

kevin: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone.
